ingredients.item: Bone-in pork country-style ribs or neck bones

instructions: Dice the onion, thinly slice the garlic and mince 1 tbsp of the parsley.
Pat the pork dry. Season it all over with 1 tsp of the salt and the pepper.

Heat the oil in a large heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the pork and sear it for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep brown. Do it in batches if the pot is crowded, then transfer the pork to a plate.
Turn the heat down to medium. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the pot, until it's soft.
Add the garlic and a pinch of red pepper flakes and cook for 2 minutes, until the garlic smells sweet.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until it darkens a little.

Add the tomatoes with their juice, the bay leaves, the parsley and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Fill one empty tomato can about a third full of water, swirl it and add it to the pot. Crush the tomatoes with the back of a spoon.
Bring the sauce to a boil. Add the pork, the sausage links whole and the meatballs. Turn the heat to low and set the lid slightly ajar.
Simmer for 3 hours, stirring every 20 minutes so the bottom doesn't scorch. It's ready when the pork is falling apart.
Remove the bay leaves and any bones. Transfer the meats to a platter and pull the pork into big pieces. Taste the sauce and add up to 1/2 tsp more salt if it needs it.
Boil a large pot of water with the last 1 tbsp of salt. Cook the spaghetti or rigatoni until it's al dente, drain it and toss it with a few ladles of sauce.
Serve the pasta with the meats and extra sauce alongside.

This makes far more sauce than tonight needs. Cool the leftover sauce and meats together and refrigerate them in sealed containers for up to 5 days, or freeze for up to 6 months. Keep any leftover pasta in a separate container. Thaw in the fridge, then reheat in a pot over medium-low heat, stirring often, with a splash of water if it has thickened.
method_notes: Coley Cooks leads (4.97 from 83): sear the pork, soften the onion, bloom the garlic and tomato paste, then a long low simmer with sausage and meatballs. A Spicy Perspective and A Family Feast show quicker or larger versions with beef, bacon and wine. The lead's ricotta and pecorino for serving are left out to keep it dairy-free, and the meatballs are fully cooked ones (the lead allows store-bought), so check the label for dairy. Most of the meat here is pork and sausage with beef meatballs; it makes enough sauce for several dinners.
